findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the customer master data uploaded to it) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.

The bucket is documented as public and has no ACL set to private, no public access block, and no bucket policy restricting access, allowing anonymous read of the sensitive customer-master.xlsx object stored in it.
No logging block is configured, so requests against a bucket holding customer data are not recorded, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorized access.

Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be overwritten or deleted (ransomware or malicious tampering) with no recoverable prior version. Combined with force_destroy = true, data destruction is irreversible.
No bucket policy denying non-TLS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests is attached, permitting cleartext HTTP access to bucket contents.

A file named customer-master.xlsx, likely containing customer PII, is uploaded to aws_s3_bucket.data which is public and unencrypted, and the object itself specifies no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial records stored unencrypted at rest with no customer-managed key control.
Although the ACL is private, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated, so a later ACL or policy change could expose financial data publicly without a guardrail.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial data, so access to it is untracked, which undermines audit requirements and breach detection.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy = true is set, so financial objects can be permanently deleted or overwritten with no recovery path.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so financial data may be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP.

The operations bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption. Any data placed in this bucket is unprotected at rest by customer-controlled keys.

No logging block is configured for the operations bucket, so object-level access to it is not recorded to the logs bucket. This removes the audit trail needed to detect or investigate unauthorised access.

The bucket relies only on a private ACL and has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy, so a later ACL or policy change could expose the bucket publicly without any account-level guardrail.
The data_science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so potentially sensitive analytics datasets are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy restricts public ACLs/policies on this bucket, leaving no defence-in-depth control against accidental public exposure.

The centralised log bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but has no public access block or bucket policy preventing public ACLs, so log data containing request metadata could be exposed by a subsequent misconfiguration.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The log bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or deletion of centralised audit logs would not itself be logged.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows Terraform to delete the bucket and all retained log objects in a single apply, undermining the integrity and availability of the audit trail.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
No bucket policy enforces aws:SecureTransport, permitting cleartext HTTP access to bucket objects.
